premises.text: Mobile device users still depend on outlets and struggle to keep phones charged through the day
premises.evidence_span: scurrying around trying to find an outlet just to get a little bit more juice in your phone

premises.text: A proprietary harvesting-antenna phone case captures wasted RF from the device and converts it to DC power that extends battery life without plugging in
premises.evidence_span: Our case is embedded with a harvesting antenna that is proprietary that captures that wasted RF energy and then takes it through a conversion process to convert it into electricity and then dumps it back into the phone

premises.text: A large share of U.S. smartphone users already buy accessories to get more phone power
premises.evidence_span: out of the 220 million smartphone users in the United States, over 30% have purchased some sort of product to help them get a little more power in their phone

premises.text: Partnership with a leading RF academic lab enables bringing the technology to market quickly
premises.evidence_span: In partnership with The Ohio State University, we have pioneered this technology and are bringing this technology to the market in less than one month from now

premises.text: The first product launches via Kickstarter
premises.evidence_span: in one month, we are launching this product. And we will be doing that on Kickstarter

value.text: Extra passive battery power for mobile devices without hunting for outlets
value.evidence_span: it works passively, and it gives you extra power that you need to get from sunup to sundown

secondary_value.text: Green recovery of wasted RF energy
secondary_value.evidence_span: It is a green technology that simply harvests wasted energy and converts it into DC power

causal_links.evidence_span: you as a consumer deserve a better solution for power for your mobile devices
extend your battery life by 30% simply using wasted energy transmitted from your phone
we are launching this product. And we will be doing that on Kickstarter

notes: Outlet-hunting and 19th-century-power framing folded as one charging-pain premise (v1.5.1 §4.1.6). Antenna, conversion, 30% extension, and no-plug vs battery-case claims folded as one RF-harvesting case mechanism with performance package (§4.1.7–8). Wireless-charger/IoT roadmap and ubiquitous-power vision treated as framing, not premises. OSU partnership kept as separately revisable tech-access condition; Kickstarter singleton retained as independently revisable launch module. Anti-template: demand, product/tech access, and launch channel separately revisable.
